assertions.name: phi_q_signed_differs_from_phi_q_abs_at_delta_scale
assertions.source: Φ_q(neg z) ≠ Φ_q(|z|) confirmed numerically at v = ±0.142

description: Concrete test of user's 2026-06-01 question: does dropping |...| in the mass-tower formula change Q_β at q_proton? Tests with specific synthetic vols lists (single positive, mixed-sign, all negative) to show when signed != abs.

findings.any_negative_vols: abs != signed — Φ_q(z) ≠ Φ_q(|z|) for negative z; the modulation factor differs structurally
findings.magnitude_of_difference: depends on |vols| · q^(-k) ratios; for small |v|<<q the difference is small (Φ_q ≈ 1 + |v|/q for both signs), but the LEADING ORDER coefficient flips sign for negative v

data.conclusion: Φ_q(z) ≠ Φ_q(|z|) for z < 0. At Δtr_M scale (|v|=0.142, q=1.11), Φ_q(-v) differs from Φ_q(+v) by ~-92.48% per term. If the framework's per-braid mass-tower uses Φ_q(|v|) but the categorical 'correct' formula should use Φ_q(v) signed, EACH negative-v term contributes a 92.48% sign-correction. Multiple negative terms compound. For PROTON / NEUTRON mass-tower: at the level of single-nucleon tr_M values (β_p ≈ +1.07, β_n ≈ +0.92), both POSITIVE, so |...| is no-op at level 0. At deeper levels (pair joints, jets) sub-braid traces CAN be negative — the |...| would change those. WHETHER THE FRAMEWORK SHOULD USE SIGNED OR ABS is a categorical question; this probe does not answer it, only quantifies that the difference is structurally meaningful when negative-v terms appear in the tower.
data.implications_for_ck_saga: Indirect — c_k saga is in BINDING (Li_2^q), not MASS (Φ_q). Q_β = m_n - m_p - m_e is a mass-DIFFERENCE; both m_n and m_p use Φ_q(|...|) in their per-braid towers. If signed-vs-abs changes m_p and m_n in correlated ways, the difference Q_β could be unchanged. Quantifying this requires the full per-isotope sub-braid V̂ values for proton and neutron — out of scope for this diagnostic. Marked as FOLLOW-UP.
